clue.text: In the '20s first silents have English director

indicators.note: In places the next letter inside the surrounding word

parts.note: a score is twenty, so the twenties are scores

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A film buff notes that cinema of the 1920s was dominated by silent pictures with English directors.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sends you to the silent-film era; Martin Scorsese is a modern American director, reached by putting S inside scores, the twenties.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is a famous American film-maker, so he is an example of a director.

clue.text: Knock back lager and lose one's balance

indicators.note: knocking something back drives it backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: Pils is a type of pale lager

explanation.surface: Down a lager too fast and you end up falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' reads naturally as drinking quickly, which fits the lager; here it signals reading the beer backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip is to lose your footing, a plain synonym for losing one's balance.

clue.text: Limp extremely painfully following odd fall at work

indicators.note: following places the earlier-mentioned piece after the pieces that come later in the clue
extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters at each end of the word

parts.note: the first and third letters of fall
op. is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: odd asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions: first, third and so on

parts.note: first and last letters of painfully

explanation.surface: Someone takes a strange fall on the job and now limps badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limp' looks like a verb about walking with an injury, but the definition is the adjective meaning slack.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp as an adjective means lacking stiffness, which is exactly what floppy describes.

clue.text: Disillusioned by New York City setback I left to travel round California

indicators.note: travelling round something encircles it, so these letters go around the next piece
something set back is turned round, so the letters run the other way

explanation.surface: After a setback in New York, someone disenchanted leaves to tour California.
explanation.walkthrough: Set back New York City, then put I and left around California.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cynical has lost faith in people's motives, which is what being disillusioned means.

clue.text: Arrange driver for reading group

parts.note: to book is to arrange or reserve
a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: Someone organises a chauffeur to take members to their reading group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a chauffeur; it is the golf club used for long tee shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A book club is a group of people who meet to discuss books they have read.

clue.text: Wicked holiday home acquires debts without number

indicators.note: acquiring something adds it on, so the following piece is attached after the first

parts.note: a villa is a rented holiday house

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so these letters sit around the next piece

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: A wicked holiday villa somehow piles up unnumbered debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: IOUS goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Villainous behaviour is that of a villain, so it is a synonym for wicked.

clue.text: Problem involving energy is electronically complex

indicators.note: something involving another thing wraps around it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A power problem turns out to be a complicated electronics issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hi-tech describes advanced technology, typically sophisticated electronic equipment.

clue.text: One church collects money to get cool treat for kids

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it on, so another piece is added to the end

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
lolly is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A church takes a collection to buy the children something nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Lolly is informal British for cash; an ice lolly is what Americans call a popsicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice lolly is frozen flavoured water on a stick, a cold sweet children love.

clue.text: God's love is supporting knight

indicators.note: a supporting piece holds up another from below or behind, so it comes after it

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A statement about divine love backing a chivalrous knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the Egyptian deity of the dead and the afterlife.

clue.text: Catch last post and raising of standard

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word after it
raising lifts the word up, turning it round so it reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: At a military ceremony, the Last Post sounds and the standard is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is a bugle call at funerals and sunset; raising the standard suggests a flag, but standard is par.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a device or trick to catch someone, and to trap is to catch.

clue.text: Dad's poorlier after doctor drops off drink with analgesic

indicators.note: after places the earlier piece behind the following one in the answer

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: dropping something off removes it, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: poorly means ill, so poorlier is iller

explanation.surface: Dad is feeling worse after the doctor leaves him a drink with a painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove DR from DRINK to leave INK; 'poorlier' is British for more unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a medicine that relieves pain, which is exactly a painkiller.

clue.text: Two leaders abandon rigour for truthfulness

indicators.note: the first two letters, the leaders, are abandoned and dropped from the word

explanation.surface: Two leaders give up strict discipline in favour of honesty.
explanation.definitionFit: Verity is a formal word for truth, the quality of being truthful or real.

clue.text: Welshman, unknown to us, runs place for scholarly retreat

parts.note: Ivor is a typically Welsh name
we is the subject form of us
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Welshman, a stranger to the speakers, runs a retreat for academics.
explanation.definitionFit: An ivory tower is a state of privileged seclusion from practical life, often said of academics.

clue.text: OK for everyone to be Tory?

parts.note: Tories belong to the political right

explanation.surface: A wry question: is it acceptable for everybody to vote Conservative?
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for Britain's Conservative Party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is a common phrase meaning acceptable or satisfactory, just like OK.

clue.text: Queen coming over to meet Irish writer's reported with delight

indicators.note: coming over suggests turning over, so the word is flipped end to end
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want how the name sounds

explanation.surface: A queen travels to meet an Irish author and is said to be delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end with 'with' as a loose link: to rejoice is to delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejoice is to feel or show great joy, which is to delight in something.

clue.text: Prize-winning French mushroom's getting good number exported

indicators.note: exported goods are sent out, so these letters are taken out of the word

explanation.surface: A prize-winning French mushroom is being shipped abroad in quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion used as an adjective describes a winner, such as a champion racehorse, so it means prize-winning.

clue.text: Wife's taking leave of girls after bad upset stomach

indicators.note: after places the earlier piece behind the following one in the answer
something upset is knocked into disorder, so these letters are jumbled
taking leave of something means departing from it, so one letter goes

explanation.surface: A wife departs a girls' outing with a bad upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset stomach' reads as one phrase, but upset belongs to bad and stomach stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach is loosely the belly, and the abdomen is the belly region of the body.

clue.text: Give opinion of cooked veal you noisily devoured

indicators.note: cooked ingredients are transformed, so these letters are rearranged
noisily means said out loud, so the word is taken for its sound

parts.note: the letter U sounds like the word

explanation.surface: A diner is asked for a verdict on the veal they wolfed down loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate is to assess or judge something, forming an opinion of its worth.

clue.text: Beat scoundrel by heading off guard

indicators.note: with its heading taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A rogue gets past a sentry by sending him away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a verb to overpower, but it is the noun for a rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a rhythmic pattern or beat, as in the rise and fall of speech or music.

clue.text: Pop star boy's young and foolish…

explanation.surface: A pop idol is described as a young, silly boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Gaga is an American singer famous for chart hits, so she is an example of a pop star.

clue.text: Once a year a nun breaks for Los Angeles retreat

indicators.note: something that breaks falls apart, so these letters are reassembled differently
retreating goes backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Once a year a nun takes a break for a retreat in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual describes something that happens yearly, every twelve months.

clue.text: bad luck his getting entangled in plot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to plot is to map out

indicators.note: entangled things get twisted into a muddle, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Misfortune strikes as he gets caught up in a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky accident, a small piece of bad luck.

clue.text: Smile about eating posh breakfast cereal

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other
about suggests moving around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone smiles as they tuck into an upmarket breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a cereal of oats, nuts and fruit, eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Short following wage cut, boy's keeping hold of money

indicators.note: keeping hold of something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other
cut means trimmed, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: After a pay cut, a lad holding on to his cash finds himself short.
explanation.definitionFit: Short in the sense of lacking something means incomplete, not having all its parts.

clue.text: Squander money when depressed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... money is British slang for spending it recklessly
second meaning: feeling down or sad

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a spending spree whenever they feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: To blue cash is an old British variant of blow it, to waste it.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue is both a slang verb for wasting money and an everyday adjective for feeling sad.

clue.text: Lay to rest in northern town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to inter a body
second meaning: a town in Greater Manchester, England

explanation.surface: Someone is buried in a town in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to place a dead body in a grave, and the proper noun is an English town.

clue.text: Stretch resources to prepare party

parts.note: to make a meal is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Hosting a party on a tight budget means making the money go far.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to manage with limited means, getting the most out of what you have.

clue.text: Those responsible for spending reductions include large public relations unit

indicators.note: to include is to take in, so the other pieces go inside

explanation.surface: Those to blame for austerity cuts include a large PR department.
explanation.definitionFit: Culprits are the people guilty of a wrongdoing, the ones to blame.
